title: Word-limit enforcement — instruct the limit in the prompt AND verify after generation; if over MAX_WORDS, trim and log a violation event (Epic 5)
prompt:
Instruct the word limit in the prompt AND verify after generation: if over MAX_WORDS, trim and log a violation event. Keep messages within the limit.

Follow repo standards: TDD (write the failing test first, then code); max 150 lines per code file (split, don't compress); ruff = 0 violations + mypy clean; no hard-coded values (read from config); every external API call goes through the API gatekeeper (Epic 13); log via the LOG package; keep coverage >= 85%. Read docs/PRD.md and the relevant docs/prds/*.md before starting.

usage.summary: usage to be filled by main loop from harness report

note: Post-generation word-limit enforcement (PRD §5.2 / §7). The PROMPT side was already done (system prompt prompts.py + per-turn anchor anchoring.py both instruct <= max_words); THIS task adds the VERIFY-AFTER-GENERATION half the engine (Epic 6) calls per turn. NEW MODULE packages/core/src/agent_debate/core/agents/word_limit.py. count_words(text) -> int defines the single counting rule: str.split() — any run of whitespace (spaces/tabs/newlines) is one separator, leading/trailing ignored, so '' and whitespace-only count as 0 words (documented + tested). enforce_word_limit(text, *, max_words, run_id=None, runs_dir=None, agent=..., round_=0) -> WordLimitResult (frozen slotted dataclass: text, violated, original_words). Within the limit — including EXACTLY max_words (edge case) and empty string — returns the text verbatim with violated=False and logs NOTHING. Over the limit: trims to EXACTLY max_words words at a clean word boundary (first max_words tokens re-joined with single spaces; no sentence-boundary heuristic — documented) and, when run_id is given, logs a violation; without run_id it still trims but skips logging. EVENT_TYPE DECISION (documented): the LOG schema's event_type Literal is {message, tool_call, nudge, timeout, retry, verdict, system} with NO 'violation' type, so a word-limit breach is logged as a 'system' event whose payload names it: {"violation": "word_limit", "words": N, "limit": max_words, "trimmed": true}. No hard-coded values: max_words is a caller param (Settings.max_words; never inlined); the event_type ('system'), log agent ('word_limit') and violation tag ('word_limit') are named constants WORD_LIMIT_LOG_EVENT_TYPE / WORD_LIMIT_LOG_AGENT / WORD_LIMIT_VIOLATION_TAG added to core.constants. API gatekeeper (Epic 13): N/A — pure text + the LOG sink, no network call. Re-exported count_words / enforce_word_limit / WordLimitResult from agent_debate.core.agents. TDD red-first: wrote packages/core/tests/test_word_limit.py FIRST, watched it fail (ImportError: count_words from agent_debate.core.agents), then implemented to green (9 tests): count_words whitespace rule + empty=0; within-limit returned unchanged with violated=False and NO violation event; exactly max_words not violated; empty string not violated; over-limit trimmed to exactly max_words (asserted count == max_words AND exact text) with violated=True; the violation logged to a tmp runs_dir JSONL as a 'system' event carrying the violation/words/limit/trimmed payload; within-limit logs no violation; no run_id still trims but writes no JSONL. Left a clean reusable seam for Epic 6 (engine calls enforce_word_limit after each debater turn); did NOT build the debate loop. Gates green locally: uv sync clean; ruff check = All checks passed; ruff format --check clean (115 files); mypy = no issues in 115 source files; pytest --cov = 462 passed, total coverage 100% (>=85); check_line_limit pass (word_limit.py well under 150 code lines); secret_scan pass. See PR CI for authoritative result.
